title: Agentic coding changes everything | Thorsten Ball from Sourcegraph Amp
summary: Sourcegraph Amp developer explains how simple agent loops are, argues for giving models tools and tokens freely, and describes generating most tests and one-off tooling with agents.

assertions.quote: And it's only 300 lines of code.

verdicts.note: Minimal agent loops (read file, list dir, run shell) are well documented to work with modern tool-calling models; production harnesses add much more but the core loop is small.

assertions.quote: So when the model gets better and bigger and stronger, the scaffolding falls away

verdicts.note: Vendors advise removing over-prescriptive instructions as models improve; but guardrails still prevent real failures. Plausible, weakly evidenced.

assertions.quote: forget about accepting each change forget about not giving the model real access to the file system.

verdicts.note: Removing per-edit approval cuts friction and works with version control and good tests; in risky environments, permission gates and sandboxing still matter.

assertions.quote: here's how you get feedback about your work. You know, here's the command you have to run to get llinter output or compiler errors

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: when have you ever become more productive with a tool after using it for just a single day? Like you have to put some effort

verdicts.note: Learning curves are real (METR's one dev with >50h Cursor experience was faster), but evidence that ramp-up reliably flips results is thin.

assertions.quote: But what to build and when and how to say organize it, how to architect it ... That's now super valuable.

verdicts.note: Plausible economic logic and widely argued, but not measured; execution, distribution and maintenance still matter.

assertions.quote: I would say the test suite 90% of that is generated, right? Like oh cover all of these cases.

verdicts.note: AI speeds drafting tests and docs, but generated tests often assert implementation details or weak properties and need review.

assertions.quote: you can build stuff that you never would have attempted before

verdicts.note: Small standalone throwaway tools are where AI generation is most reliable, and many practitioners report building debugging aids they previously skipped.

assertions.quote: people change the code base to leverage AI more.

verdicts.note: Clear structure and smaller units plausibly help agents (and humans), but controlled evidence on how much restructuring improves agent results is thin.

assertions.quote: if you work on a distributed storage layer at Google an agent is not going to take your job in the next two years

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.
